newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka Employees Fund bids for bank stake.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka Employees Fund bids for bank stake.

text.p: The Employees Trust Fund (ETF) has made a bid for a 40 percent equity stake in Commercial Bank Ltd, currently held by Standard Chartered Bank, the fund said in statement on Friday.
The stake, the single largest holding in Commercial Bank, has been on the market for over two years.
Hatton National Bank Ltd and Development Finance Corporation of Ceylon Ltd, have also expressed interest in buying the stake.
Commercial Bank has said it would prefer to link up with DFCC, a development bank.
It said a merger with Hatton National, a direct competitor, could lead to the closure of many branches and possible staff redundencies and less competition.
On Friday, Hatton National Bank aid: "We can assure the staff of Commercial Bank that the question of closure of any of the branches or retrenchment of their staff will not arise."
The final decision, however, lies with the Central Bank and the Takeovers and Mergers Code of the Securities & Exchange Commission (SEC) which regulates the stock market.
According to Sri Lankan laws, a single organisation cannot own more than 15 percent in a banking institution, while for individuals the limit is 10 percent.
The Takeovers and Mergers Code comes into play whenever between 30 and 50 percent of the equity of a listed company changes hands.
The code says that the buyer has to make a similar offer to minority shareholders of the company, and the whole transaction has to go through the floor of the stock exchange.
